title: GNSS spoofing signatures in real AIS tracks: detectors, injected ground truth, GeoJSON and CoT
summary: Shore-side detection of GNSS spoofing from the AIS picture, on real Danish Maritime Authority AIS (partial HTTP-range download of a daily file, ~4.4 h, 1.7 M fixes, 2.5-3 k vessels). Stdlib detectors for teleports, vessel-type speed limits, position-derived vs reported SOG/COG/heading, turn radius vs ship length, loitering-while-underway, crop-circle clusters of vessels on one point, on-land positions (Natural Earth 10m, eroded) and MMSI anomalies including one MMSI on two transmitters. Offset, drift, single-circle and group crop-circle episodes are injected into real tracks to measure recall and time-to-detect (offsets >= 2 km and circles ~0.9-1.0 recall, median TTD 5-17 s; slow 1-2 m/s drift ~0.1). Alerts on unaltered data are broken down by hand (coastline artifacts, a real MMSI conflict, an inland Class B report). pyais handles raw NMEA decode and an encode/decode round trip; flagged vessels export as GeoJSON and Cursor-on-Target via the mavlink-to-tak-cot builder. Public incidents (Black Sea 2017, C4ADS 2019, SkyTruth 2025, Baltic 2025) are cited.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06: run.py with python 3.12.14 (pyais 3.3.1, pandas 3.1.1, shapely 2.2.0, pyshp 3.1.6) on DMA AIS 2026-11-03 and 2026-10-20 (first ~100 MB of each zip), 3 injection seeds per day, plus a pyais NMEA encode/decode round trip with identical scores; nmea_io.py stats on the pyais tests/nmea-sample file; 19 stdlib unit tests pass on python 3.14.7, and disabling the jump, cluster, turn, on-land or SOG checks makes tests fail. Not done: CoT shown in an ATAK/WinTAK client, live NMEA stream ingestion (Kystverket stream unreachable from this network), NOAA MarineCadastre data. No real spoofing event was found in the 8.8 h analysed; detection numbers come from injected episodes.
